units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 1:6">Targ. Y. Deut. I, 6</cite> (v., however, <cite ref="A03062"><he>אֲרַח</he></cite>).—

<cite ref="Shabbat 134a:14">Sabb. 134ᵃ</cite> <he>לִיתְרְחוּ ליה וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>לישתהי</he>; Ar. <he>לִיתְרְהוּ</he>) let them wait with his circumcision, until the blood withdraws from the surface. Ib. 136ᵃ <he>אי אִיתְרְחִיתוּ ליה וכ׳</he> if you had waited until evening to kill it, we should have eaten of it.
<cite ref="Moed Katan 28a:22">M. Kat. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>אִיתְרַח לי וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>איתרך</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) give me thirty days’ time.
<cite ref="Arakhin 9a">Arakh. 9ᵃ</cite> <he>קא מִתְרְהָא סיהרא וכ׳</he> Ar. (Var. <he>מתאחר</he>) the new month would be delayed two (three) days; (ed. <he>מייתרא</he> the old month would gain &c.).

<cite ref="Niddah 30b:19">Nidd. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>אתרח ארבעין יומין וכ׳</he> Var. (read: <cite ref="T00242"><he>אִתְרְחָא</he></cite>; ed. <he>אייתרה</he>) she may have waited forty days and then become pregnant; a. e.—

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 80b:1">B. Kam. 80ᵇ</cite> <he>מאן נִתְרַח ניתרח וכ׳</he> (Rashi to <cite ref="Gittin 68b:14">Gitt. 68ᵇ</cite> <he>מאן תרח ניתרח</he>) who shall wait (in the antechamber)? shall Samuel wait, and Rab and R. Asi enter?; <he>ונתרח רב או רב אסי</he> but should Rab have waited or Rab Asi? [Ms. M. <he>מאן טרח ניטרח וכ׳</he> who should be troubled? &c.]
Gitt. 68ᵇ תַּרֲחֵיה גביה וכ׳ (Ar. תַּרְהֲיֵיה Paeli) he kept him with him until &c.

senses.gloss: to be liberal. Y. B. Mets. VI, beg. 10ᵈ לא דאנא … אלא אנא חייה מַתְרִיחַ לכון (ed. Krot. מתרית, corr. acc.) not that I am legally bound to give you your wages, but I, Ḥiya, am liberal towards you.

units: Ab. Zar. 18ᵃ מַתְרַחְנָא מִתְרַח (not מרתח; Ms. M. מתרחנא only; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) I will give you time (wait until you are well again); [prob. to be read: מַרְתַּחְנָא I am hot, v. רְתַה.]
